2.critique: Previous round. The clearest h and the best small-size survival, because the h is plain and the dot-and-bar do the family work. But the m and the negative-space trick are absent: it is the original's dot and bar bolted on.

3.critique: Previous round. The plus joint is a real echo of overlapping bars, and it reads h at 32px, but it is heavy, closes up at 16px, and says nothing about m.

6.critique: Fails. The arch poking out of the stem plus a second arch reads as a lowercase m (or 'tm' at 32px); the ascender is too short against the width to win. The m dominates, so h is not the primary read.

7.critique: Works as a concept: the h reads (ascender, wide shoulder, leg) and the two white slots either side of the peg make an m you only see on a second look, the way the original's two white lobes read B. Costs: it is wide (253 by 235), the slots are 40 units so they fill in below about 24px, and at 16px it is an h with a blob.

8.critique: Fails the brief. It is the original M with a taller left stem, and it reads M first and h second. Kept to show why: a V cannot be an arch.

9.critique: A clear h at 32px with a period. The J hook is a nice private joke on the stem's foot, but it is a flag more than a hook at small sizes, and the dot makes it 'h.' rather than 'h!'. No m in it.

10.critique: The strongest h of the new set: tall stem, pointed shoulder, one leg, compact (166 by 235), and it holds at 16px. The shoulder is made of the original's two diagonals turned over, so the M is there for anyone who knows the old mark, but nothing in it is an m on its own.

11.critique: Clear h at every size, and the floating dot rhymes with the original's dot. But it is only an h with a dot; the dot reads as an apostrophe or a stray mark, and there is no m.

12.critique: Reads 'hm' with two dots, busy at 32px, muddy at 16px. The idea (a hanging '!' inside the m) is too clever for the size.

13.critique: The peg inside a steep ridge is the closest this gets to the original's layering (M diagonals positive, m in the white slots), and at large size it is rewarding. At 32px the peg fuses with the ridge and the mark is a lumpy h with no visible slots. Too much going on in a 235-unit square.

14.critique: The best answer to 'incorporate the m more': two ridges over three stems, so it is h and m at once, built only from the original's diagonals and stems. Risk: the m wins at a glance and a stranger may read 'hm' or 'm'. The ascender saves it at 32px; at 16px it is a small m with a tall stem.

15.critique: Fails at small sizes: hook, ridge and dot compete and the mark is about 340 wide so the tile shrinks it. Three layers but not one clear read.
